subject: physics_2
question_text: Derive an expression for the energy stored in a capacitor.

verification.note: The 1+1+1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Two structural checks are IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the two-book union check (the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only) and the past-paper back-test (the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers). Hand-checked: the book's average-potential route is correct because V rises linearly with q (V = q/C), so the mean of 0 and V is V/2 and W = (V/2)Q = QV/2; with Q = CV this is CV²/2 = Q²/2C, matching the integral route the LAQ uses. Printed question text carries no error.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

steps.label: The set-up
lines: Take an uncharged capacitor of capacitance C.
Its charge and its potential difference are both
zero to begin with. It is now connected across a
Let the final potential difference between the
plates be V and the final charge be Q = CV.
steps.margin_note: First mark. Start from zero charge and name the final Q and V.
steps.why: The energy is the work done during the charging, so the answer has to start at zero charge — starting from the fully charged state leaves nothing to integrate.
common_mistakes: Starting with the capacitor already charged, so no work is left to count.
Writing U = QV instead of QV/2 by forgetting that V grows from zero.

recall.must_convey: That an uncharged capacitor C is charged by a battery to a final charge Q and a final potential difference V.
accept: charge it with a battery to Q and V
reject: average potential difference is V by 2

steps.memory_tip: The energy equals the work done while charging, so start the count from zero charge.

steps.label: The average potential difference
lines: While the capacitor charges, the potential
difference rises steadily from 0 to V, because
at any stage it equals q/C and q grows steadily.
So the average potential difference is
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The rise is steady, so the mean of 0 and V is V/2.
steps.why: V is proportional to q, so the graph of V against q is a straight line through the origin and its average height over the charging is exactly half the final height.
common_mistakes: Taking the average as V, which doubles the answer.
Not saying why the average is V/2 — the steady rise is the reason.

recall.must_convey: That the potential difference rises steadily from 0 to V, so the average value is V/2.
accept: average potential difference is V by 2
V rises steadily so take half
reject: work is average V times Q

steps.memory_tip: A straight rise from 0 to V has an average of V/2 — half the final value.

steps.label: The work done
lines: The work done in moving the total charge Q at
This work is stored in the capacitor as
electric potential energy U, so U = QV/2.
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Multiply the average V by the total Q and call the result U.
steps.why: Work equals charge times the potential difference it is moved through; using the average value is what makes the single multiplication correct for a rising V.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by the final V instead of the average V.
Stopping at W without saying it is stored as potential energy U.

recall.must_convey: That the work is the average potential difference times the total charge, QV/2, and it is stored as U.
accept: work is average V times Q
this work is stored as potential energy
reject: U is Q squared by 2 C

steps.memory_tip: Work = total charge × the average potential difference.

steps.label: The three forms
lines: Substituting Q = CV, the same energy can be
Use CV²/2 when V is given and Q²/2C when the
steps.margin_note: Last mark. All three forms, then say which one to pick.
steps.why: Q = CV lets any one of Q, C and V be eliminated, so one stored quantity is enough to find the energy in any problem.
common_mistakes: Writing CV² or Q²/C and dropping the factor of two.
Giving only one form when the question asks for the expression.

recall.must_convey: That U = QV/2 = CV²/2 = Q²/2C, the three equivalent forms.
accept: U is half C V squared
U is Q squared by 2 C
reject: average potential difference is V by 2

steps.memory_tip: Q = CV replaces any one of the three letters, so one formula gives three forms.

insider_note: The mark that goes missing is the factor of two: an answer that writes U = QV or CV² has skipped the average-potential line, and the examiner reads that line before the final box.
